keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Coburg passed in 1347 to the Wettins through Catherine of Henneberg's marriage to Frederick III of Meissen. Revised after review: the 1360 inheritance treaty did not take Schmalkalden from the county. The Schmalkalden page: 'When the Counts of Henneberg became extinct in 1583, their share was inherited by William IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel'; the German page on the House of Henneberg: 'Damit wurde das hennebergisch-hessische Kondominium begründet' (1360). The county keeps its share to 1583, so the 1360 keyframe is merged into this one (1347-1582).

ledger.note: About 1037 (infobox 'c. 1037-1660'; the page ties no event to the year). Poppo I is the first count, with no year; 'in 1096, Count Godebold II of Henneberg served as a burgrave of the Würzburg bishops' and his father Poppo 'had been killed in battle in 1078'. Review follow-up: the infobox 'c. 1037' is not confirmed by the German page on the House of Henneberg, which gives Poppo I's first mention as 1078 (chronicle) and 1096 (charter) and says the family founded the county 'toward the end of the 11th century'; the year 1037 stays at confidence 1 as the infobox's, and the pages disagree.
1247: Schmalkalden. Count Herman I received the lordship 'in 1247 from Henry III of Meissen'. (It lies inside the stand-in circle.)
1248: Coburg. The counts 'inherited it in 1248 after the Andechs line ended.'
1274: three branches. 'In 1274 the Henneberg estates were divided into the Schleusingen, Aschach-Römhild and Hartenberg branches.' Entered as a dynastic step inside one state.
1310: princely count. 'Their county was raised to a princely county in 1310.'
1347: Coburg to the Wettins. Coburg 'passed to the Wettins through Catherine of Henneberg's marriage to Frederick III of Meissen' (the page gives no 1353 transfer).

1583: the Henneberg share of Schmalkalden goes to Hesse-Kassel. Schmalkalden page: 'When the Counts of Henneberg became extinct in 1583, their share was inherited by William IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel'. The 1360 event is the treaty, not the transfer: County page 'The Lordship of Schmalkalden fell to Landgrave William IV of Hesse-Kassel, according to an inheritance treaty of 1360' (William IV ruled from 1567); the German page on the House of Henneberg dates the Henneberg-Hesse condominium to 1360 and adds that after 1583 there was a dispute with Hesse-Kassel over the 'Doppelherrschaft Schmalkalden'. The earlier version entered a 1360 loss to landgraviate-of-hesse at confidence 3.

region.text: the Henneberg share of the lordship of Schmalkalden

ledger.note: 1583: the last count. 'The last count, George Ernest, died in 1583, ending the line.' Both the Ernestine and Albertine Wettin branches claimed the estates; the infobox ends the county in 1660, when they were divided among Saxe-Weimar, Saxe-Gotha and Maurice of Saxe-Zeitz. In 1554 William IV had signed an inheritance treaty with John Frederick II of Saxony. Revised after review: the Schmalkalden circle is not handed to Saxony (the dissolve region excludes it) but to Hesse-Kassel in the preceding event. The German page on the House of Henneberg gives the shares of the claim: 'Den Ernestinern (Weimar/Gotha) standen sieben, den Albertinern (Dresden) fünf Zwölftel der Erbmasse zu', under the 1554 Kahla treaty that provided for Saxony's takeover of Henneberg when the line died out.

certainty.note: The page gives no area; the circle is a stand-in and the dated acquisitions of Ilmenau (1343) and Meiningen (1542) lie inside it. Schmalkalden was a Henneberg-Hesse condominium from 1360, so its border is soft.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Henneberg row.

SCOPE. The infobox span is c. 1037-1660; the county's last count died in 1583, and 1583-1660 is a Wettin condominium, so the state ends at 1583 with the Saxon rows as counterpart (flagged at confidence 2). Other dated items, all inside the circle: Ilmenau purchased 1343, Meiningen (a Würzburg fief) acquired 1542, the 1554 inheritance treaty with John Frederick II of Saxony. The 1815 passage of the Albertine parts round Schleusingen and Suhl to Prussia's Province of Saxony is after the state. Counterpart years for Schmalkalden are those of the Henneberg page; the Hesse-Kassel named there is the landgraviate-of-hesse of the time.

SHAPES. Main circle 10.65E 50.55N 28 km; Coburg 10.96E 50.26N 12 km; Schmalkalden 10.45E 50.72N 10 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Schleusingen', 'Meiningen', 'Suhl', 'Schmalkalden', 'Römhild', 'Coburg', 'Ilmenau'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The 1037 start has no event on the page; (2) no area; (3) the page's 1353 and 1291 Coburg dates are not on it (the 1347 transfer is); (4) the War of the Thuringian Succession is named without dates.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). (1) Schmalkalden: the 1360 loss to landgraviate-of-hesse is removed. The County page says it 'fell to Landgrave William IV of Hesse-Kassel, according to an inheritance treaty of 1360'; the Schmalkalden page says 'When the Counts of Henneberg became extinct in 1583, their share was inherited by William IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel'; the German page on the House of Henneberg dates the Henneberg-Hesse condominium to 1360. So the county keeps its share (keyframes merged, 1347-1582) and loses it in 1583 to landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel (confidence 3 for the year, the Schmalkalden page's). The dissolve already excluded the Schmalkalden circle from the Saxon hand-over; the Hessian share is now an event and a successor. landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel (verdict fix, not touched) has no 1583 gain of Schmalkalden and needs one. (2) The main circle also covered Schmalkalden before 1247; it is cut out until 1246 (new 1247 keyframe). (3) 1037 stays confidence 1: the German page on the House of Henneberg gives 1078/1096 and 'toward the end of the 11th century', not 1037; the page 'Henneberger' is silent. (4) The Saxon hand-over: Ernestines seven twelfths, Albertines five twelfths (German page); the 1660 division is in the infobox.
